text:
Casey Mittelstadt has 9 goals in 25 games, and that number has Boston talking about what comes next for him. NBC Sports Boston asked it outright: "How does Mittelstadt's hot start to season impact future with Bruins?" He's playing under 15 minutes a night, mostly in a middle-six role, and scoring like a top-line forward.

We'd be careful with the pace. The 9 goals came on 4.9 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and he's shooting 27%, up from 19% last season, which was already high. The Bruins have also scored 6.2 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Very little of that tends to last a full season.

What should last is the playmaking. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 81st percentile among forwards in primary shot assists last season, and Boston gets 54% of the expected goals with him on at five on five. He scored in Friday's loss to Toronto, his fourth goal in the last ten. Our range for his season sits at 16 to 26 goals: a good year, with the finishing coming back to earth.
